To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. The positive-only framework of the ILP system CProgol can generate a Chomsky-like context free grammar that is useful for recognising members of a family of proteins known as Human Neuropeptide Precursors (NPP).

1) CProgol can be used for learning a grammar that is useful for filtering a class of biological sequences; 2) The grammar can be used as a feature set in a classifier that is significantly more accurate than the grammar alone; 3) Searching for new human neuropeptide precursor genes is more than 10,000 times more efficient than using random selection.

(1) the CProgol positive-only learning framework is a powerful tool for learning accurate comprehensable grammars from positive examples alone and (2) the grammar representations are useful in learning accurate predictors of NPPs and that the use of these representations can lead to a significant reduction in the cost of searching for NPP sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of ILP to generate grammars for recognising members of a biological sequence family, and to show that the use of grammar-derived features improves the performance of the resulting predictor.
learning a model which can be used to recognise a class of proteins.
the development of new techniques for the discovery of biological sequence families using positive examples alone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a grammar for NPP recognition is useful for improving the performance of a predictor of NPPs.
our results support the hypothesis that the use of grammar representations can be useful for learning accurate and comprehensible predictors of biological sequence families.
our results support the use of Chomsky-like grammars for biological sequence families.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a Chomsky-like representation for NPPs has been shown to improve both accuracy and efficiency in the prediction of NPPs and the generation of a comprehensible grammar.
the use of grammar-derived features can significantly improve the predictive accuracy and RA of a predictor of NPP proteins.
Chomsky-like grammars are a useful representation for learning comprehensible predictors for members of biological sequence classes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Chomsky-like grammars, and the positive-only learning approach, can be used for modelling real-world scientific phenomena, where they can provide a significant advantage over other approaches.
, when positives are rare, it can be more effective to learn a predictor from the grammar than to learn a predictor directly from the data.
, when positives are rare, a grammar can provide a more efficient and more effective way to learn a predictor than using a feature set that is not derived from the grammar.
